program: Civil legal aid for housing, safety, benefits and economic security
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: Lone Star Legal Aid provides free civil legal assistance to eligible low-income people in Texas and southwest Arkansas.
It handles housing, family safety, public benefits, consumer, disaster and employment matters.
Our initial model examines a conditional legal-safety and household-resource channel, including costs to public-benefit payers.
strengths: Legal barriers can affect both health and net household resources.
The 2024 original return and recipient report agree on annual cost and identify native case outputs.
Explicit payer losses prevent treating transfers as free economic gains.
reservations: Cases and individuals are not distinct successful households, and categories overlap.
The reported economic awards and savings are not causal net consumption or all new government benefits.
Houston share, additional outcomes and health effects are unmeasured hypotheses; marginal donation response is unknown.

sections.what: Lone Star Legal Aid provides free civil legal assistance to eligible low-income people in Texas and southwest Arkansas. It handles housing, family safety, public benefits, consumer, disaster and employment matters. Our initial model examines a conditional legal-safety and household-resource channel, including costs to public-benefit payers.
sections.monitoring: Request deduplicated Houston households, case outcomes versus alternative aid, source and timing of awards, benefits displaced and payer costs. The 2024 report gives 25,111 cases and 61,289 individuals; current homepage gives 2025 27,973 cases and 67,153 individuals, not matched to the cost used here. The annual-reports heading says 2025 but links the 2024 body. A newer audit was reported available but not retrieved; no 2025 cost is claimed.
sections.qualitative: Legal barriers can affect both health and net household resources. The 2024 original return and recipient report agree on annual cost and identify native case outputs. Explicit payer losses prevent treating transfers as free economic gains. Cases and individuals are not distinct successful households, and categories overlap. The reported economic awards and savings are not causal net consumption or all new government benefits. Houston share, additional outcomes and health effects are unmeasured hypotheses; marginal donation response is unknown. Operating legal recipient EIN 74-1537787. Official donation page supports Lone Star Legal Aid, not similarly named justice organizations. The 76-county Texas/Arkansas service area is larger than Houston.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $22.50 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 7.186068 clinical QALYs and 12.109496 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.004444 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $43,421,735. Annual 2024 25,111 case opportunities × uniqueness 0.8 × incremental outcome 0.3 gives 6,026.64 exposed households. A judged clinical subgroup of one quarter of the case cohort, response 0.3, yields 451.998 health responders at utility 0.02 for two years after a one-year delay. This is a conditional safety/stress hypothesis, not measured legal clinical efficacy. Full 0.0005 QALY harm and $50 burden apply to all exposed households. A 25% resource response gets one-year $2,000 benefit/settlement resources, $500 disposable work resources and $100 actual otherwise-paid household medical savings; positive overlap 0.5 applies before one log. Houston share 0.5 is a judgment. Union 6026.64 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 451.998; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. The $2,000 benefit hypothesis is not a calibration to the reported $15.3 million awards/savings, which includes unlike categories and stocks. Central $1,000 payer loss per successful household assumes half of the transfer is public-funded; this mix is judgment. Full transfer incidence tests $2,000 payer loss. Dispersed 100,000 distinct payer households at $50,000 baseline bear the full transfer cost for Houston-attributed recipients: local share is applied once to the recipient-linked amount, then payer pathway editionShare 1. No second Houston haircut removes that cost. Work resources are net of taxes, benefit withdrawal and recurring work expenses; access costs remain separate. Counterparty losses, job displacement and other provider costs have adverse cases. Central external partner costs remain unknown-neutral; the central public-payer loss is explicitly included, not assumed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: State and federal grants fund most work. Official services warn eligible applicants may receive advice or brief service rather than full representation; eligibility is not completed outcome. Unrestricted donation capacity remains unknown.

model.costScope: Whole FY 2024 annual legal recipient cost versus one conditional legal-safety and signed-resources channel; not complete portfolio or marginal gift EV.
model.geographicAttribution: Seventy-six counties across Texas and southwest Arkansas; judged Houston share 0.5, not all statewide clients.
model.formula: Health = (clinicalN × unique × b × clinicalResponse × q × finite discounted duration − N × unique × b × union harm discounted at onset) × edition share. Income = signed joint household log welfare equivalents with positive-only overlap and full costs. Better-life cost = 10 × full annual cost / (health + income), only when combined benefits are positive.
model.counterfactual: Public-funded aid, pro bono and alternative legal providers, self-help, existing benefit eligibility and case resolution retained; only incremental outcomes count.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Cases, people and economic awards/savings are descriptive outputs, not measured causal QALYs or disposable-income gains.
